content.key_idea: Octopus trades full connectivity for a sparse, islanded topology: dense intra-island CXL links give low-latency communication at small scale, while a separate set of external MPDs interconnects islands to still enable large-scale memory pooling.
content.reading_order: left column reads baseline topologies top to bottom (a) Fully-connected MPD then (b) CXL Switch; right side shows the larger (c) Octopus sparse topology with islands and external MPDs

summary: Figure 1 compares three CXL memory-pod topologies. (a) A Fully-connected MPD pod wires every server (S0-S3) to every memory pooling device (P0-P7) directly. (b) A CXL Switch pod instead routes all servers (S0-S19) through a single CXL Switch to reach the MPDs (P0-P9), trading full connectivity for switch-mediated sharing. (c) Octopus's sparse topology organizes 96 servers and 192 MPDs into six islands (Island 0...Island 5), each with 16 servers densely wired to 20 island-specific MPDs (brown links) to guarantee pairwise MPD overlap for low-latency intra-island communication, while a separate set of 72 external MPDs (navy links) interconnects the islands to provide the expansion needed for effective memory pooling across the whole pod. The figure visually contrasts full/switched connectivity against Octopus's islands-plus-external-MPD design.
